Lessons.Title: Graphing the Standard Form (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: investigate how the coefficient a of x² and constant c affect graphs of y=ax²+c through controlled parameter changes, and distinguish vertical intercept, opening direction and width. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L12 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/12/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/12/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source has actual technology-driven graph manipulation; written examples here are not claimed as performed software operations.

Original family A(x)=2x²+3, B(x)=−x²+3, C(x)=(1/2)x²+3. Each has y-intercept(0,3), but A and C open upward while B opens downward. All have vertex at(0,3) in this special b=0 family. At x2, outputs A11,B−1,C5, showing coefficient magnitude changes vertical distance from vertex.

Compare widths: when a>0, larger |a| produces a steeper/narrower parabola than smaller |a| at equal horizontal distance from vertex. The negative sign reflects opening without changing the y-intercept. If c rises from3 to7 while a is fixed2, all outputs rise4 and the vertex shifts vertically to(0,7), without horizontal change.

Student task: generate a common-axis sketch and, if actually available, use graphing technology to vary a and c separately; predict effect before seeing graph and explain which features remain invariant. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for sampled output values, correct opening/width, vertical shift and truthful representation of graphing technology use.

KeyConcepts.Title: Coefficient a
KeyConcepts.Definition: In ax²+c, sign of a determines opening and |a| controls vertical stretch.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare at x equidistant from zero.

KeyConcepts.Title: Constant c
KeyConcepts.Definition: For ax²+c, y-intercept and vertex output are c.

KeyConcepts.Title: Parameter isolation
KeyConcepts.Definition: To infer effects, change only one coefficient at a time.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Hold a fixed to see c shift.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare three outputs
WorkedExamples.Question: Evaluate A,B,C at x2.
WorkedExamples.Method: Evaluate explicit first-party quadratic coefficients and check graph features via algebra.
Steps: The distinct x2 outputs reveal opening/stretch.

WorkedExamples.Title: Analyze opening and vertex
WorkedExamples.Question: Find vertex for each y=ax²+3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Evaluate explicit first-party quadratic coefficients and check graph features via algebra.
Steps: For positive a≥0, x² is nonnegative, so value at0 is minimum.
For B negative a, x² term nonpositive, so value at0 is maximum.
Thus all vertices at(0,3), but their extrema directions differ.

WorkedExamples.Title: Shift constant term
WorkedExamples.Question: What changes replacing A=2x²+3 by D=2x²+7?
WorkedExamples.Method: Evaluate explicit first-party quadratic coefficients and check graph features via algebra.
Steps: Subtract expressions D−A=4 at every x.
The vertical intercept changes from3 to7.
The parabola retains its shape and opening.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming a change in c shifts graph sideways
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Constant addition changes outputs, not inputs.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Calling smaller coefficient a a faster/narrower graph
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: For same x displacement, smaller |a| yields smaller vertical change.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Asserting graphical technology interaction without evidence
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A numerical text table is not an executed graphing session.

SummaryPoints: For y=ax²+c, a controls opening/steepness and c controls vertical position.
All original examples share vertex(0,3) and intercept3.
Changing c translates vertically while retaining shape.
Teacher assesses graph observations and truthful technology evidence.
